'''Alejandra Melfo''' (born 26 February 1965) is a Uruguayan-born Venezuelan physicist. She is known for her efforts studying and conserving glaciers, especially the [[Pico Humboldt#Glaciers|Humboldt Corona]], the last glacier in Venezuela.

== Early life ==
Melfo was born in [[Montevideo]], the Uruguayan capital, and moved to Venezuela with her family in 1976 as [[Civic-military dictatorship of Uruguay|refugees from dictatorship]] when she was 11.<ref name="atlantic">{{cite web|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2019/01/last-glacier-venezuela/579613/|title=The Scientific Cost of Glacial Retreat in Venezuela: Watching Venezuela's Last Glacier Disappear|last1=Gutiérrez|first1=Jeanfreddy|last2=Rodríguez|first2=María Fernanda|date=15 January 2019|website=The Atlantic|access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref> She later became a naturalized Venezuelan citizen.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://webdelprofesor.ula.ve/ciencias/melfo/Prof/Principal_files/vitae.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae|last=Melfo|first=Alejandra|publisher=[[University of the Andes (Venezuela)|University of the Andes]]|pages=1–7|access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref> She studied at the [[University of the Andes (Venezuela)|University of the Andes]] (ULA) in [[Mérida, Mérida|Mérida]] and received her undergraduate degree in 1989, her master's degree in 1994, and became a faculty member at ULA whilst studying for a PhD in astrophysics at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] (SISSA) in [[Trieste]], Italy.<ref name="atlantic"/><ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
[[File:Glacial_Pico_Humboldt_4.JPG|thumb|La Corona glacier, close to disappearing, has appeared recurrently in the works of Melfo.]]
At the University of the Andes, Melfo has worked in the Department of Physics and as director of the Center for Fundamental Physics. She has contributed to more than twenty scientific publications since the early 1990s.<ref name=":0" />

Originally working on [[supersymmetric theory]],<ref name="atlantic"/> her work later became focused on the deterioration of glaciers, specifically [[Pico Humboldt#Glaciers|La Corona]], the last glacier in Venezuela,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sierranevadademerida.com/picohumboldtyglaciarlacorona/|title=Pico Humboldt y Glaciar la Corona|website=Sierra Nevada de Mérida|language=Spanish|access-date=12 March 2019|date=2016-03-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sierranevadademerida.com/solo-queda-el-1-del-glaciar-la-corona-en-el-pico-humboldt-segun-la-nasa/|title=Solo queda el 1 % del Glaciar la Corona en el Pico Humboldt según la NASA|website=Sierra Nevada de Mérida|language=Spanish|access-date=12 March 2019|date=2018-11-28|archive-date=2019-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401152226/https://www.sierranevadademerida.com/solo-queda-el-1-del-glaciar-la-corona-en-el-pico-humboldt-segun-la-nasa/|url-status=dead}}</ref> after being introduced to the research of Andrés Yarzábal, a microbiologist at the University of the Andes.<ref name="atlantic"/> Melfo is the leader of a group of scientists who are dedicated to studying the disappearance of ice forms due to climate change.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://efectococuyo.com/la-humanidad/el-ultimo-glaciar-de-venezuela-no-tiene-quien-lo-estudie/|title=El último glaciar de Venezuela no tiene quién lo estudie|last=Gutiérrez|first=Jeanfreddy|date=26 November 2018|website=Efecto Cocuyo|language=Spanish|access-date=12 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401150842/http://efectococuyo.com/la-humanidad/el-ultimo-glaciar-de-venezuela-no-tiene-quien-lo-estudie/|archive-date=1 April 2019}}</ref>

She has also undertaken fieldwork while researching glaciers, fronting an expedition to the [[Pico Bolívar#Glacial retreat|Pico Bolívar glacier]]. She undertook training in climbing for months before traveling to the glacier, which has since melted completely. This is one of two expeditions from which 600 largely previously unknown microbial strains were recovered to be studied at the university, where they are preserved in deep freezers.<ref name="atlantic"/>

=== Post-retirement ===
Melfo officially retired in 2016 but has continued to work through [[Crisis in Venezuela|Venezuela's crisis]] as other academics, including the majority of her Vida Glacial project team, leave. The remaining scientists face difficulties with their work, primarily with keeping the samples frozen amid blackouts.<ref name="atlantic"/> Though Melfo is disturbed by the disappearance of the glaciers, she knows that with samples collected research can continue for a long time,<ref name="atlantic"/> and also believes that new ecosystems developing on the site of former glaciers will be "beautiful to see".<ref name="C21"/> She has also called the disappearance of glaciers a reminder of humanity's responsibility to look after the planet and to attempt to slow down climate change.<ref name="C21">{{cite web|url=https://claves21.com.ar/venezuela-primer-pais-del-mundo-en-quedarse-sin-glaciares/|title=Venezuela, primer país del mundo en quedarse sin glaciares|last=Rodríguez|first=Érika|date=25 September 2018|website=Revista Claves21|language=Spanish|access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref>

She worked with her cousin,<ref name="TEC">{{cite web|url=http://www.todoelcampo.com.uy/prima_de_jorge_drexler_expone_su_clara_vision_sobre_lo_que_sucede_en_venezuela-15?nid=11330|title=Prima de Jorge Drexler expone su clara visión sobre lo que sucede en Venezuela|date=24 February 2014|website=Todo el Campo|language=Spanish|access-date=1 April 2019|archive-date=1 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401215150/http://www.todoelcampo.com.uy/prima_de_jorge_drexler_expone_su_clara_vision_sobre_lo_que_sucede_en_venezuela-15?nid=11330}}</ref> the Uruguayan musician [[Jorge Drexler]], to write the song "Despedir a los glaciares", which is included on the 2017 album ''Salavidas de hielo'' and is about the disappearance of the glaciers and the problems that cause it.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.discogs.com/es/Jorge-Drexler-Salvavidas-de-Hielo/release/10997074|title=Salvavidas de hielo de Jorge Drexler|date=22 September 2017 |publisher=discogs|language=Spanish|access-date=12 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.noticias.com.ve/jorge-drexler-habla-sobre-el-ultimo-glaciar-de-venezuela|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181130144038/http://www.noticias.com.ve/jorge-drexler-habla-sobre-el-ultimo-glaciar-de-venezuela/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=November 30, 2018|title=Esta canción de Jorge Drexler habla sobre el último glaciar de Venezuela|date=28 November 2018|website=Noticias ve|language=Spanish|access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref> Also in 2017, she was one of the jury deciding the recipients of the [[Lorenzo Mendoza Fleury Science Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globovision.com/article/fundacion-empresas-polar-anuncio-ganadores-de-la-xviii-edicion-del-premio-lorenzo-mendoza-fleury|title=Fundación Empresas Polar anunció ganadores de la XVIII edición del Premio Lorenzo Mendoza Fleury|date=27 April 2017|website=Globovision|language=Spanish|access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref>

In 2019 Melfo and biology students of the University of the Andes began working with the [[Global Observation Research Initiative in Alpine Environments|GLORIA-Andes Project]], focusing on the effects of climate change on biodiversity from high-altitude climates. They again face problems being unable to use computers for notes due to a lack of printing ink, and relying on [[second-hand]] or donated climbing gear that they store in a [[Local Committees for Supply and Production|CLAP]] box.<ref name="atlantic"/>

== Personal life ==
Melfo disagrees with the [[Presidency of Nicolás Maduro|Maduro administration]]. She wrote a famous 2014 letter to Drexler that was widely published in Uruguay, where she explains her feelings towards the crisis in Venezuela, especially the [[Tupamaro (Venezuela)|tupamaros]] of Mérida, and her reasons for participating in the [[2014 Venezuelan protests]].<ref name="TEC"/>
